about.title: About the data
about.what: Roshni shows the load-shedding schedules that IESCO and K-Electric publish, and the planned shutdowns IESCO announces in press releases. These are plans, not measurements: a feeder listed as scheduled may have had power, and a feeder not listed may not have.
about.levels: IESCO publishes a playbook: one schedule for each interruption level (2 to 12 hours a day). Its files never say which level is in force, so this site never assumes one. You choose the level.
about.time: All times are Pakistan Standard Time (Asia/Karachi, UTC+5, no daylight saving). A window such as 22:35–02:05 crosses midnight; the end minute is not included.
about.matching: Feeders are matched to census localities and press-release names by name only. A match's percentage is the name similarity after ignoring case, spacing and punctuation; 100% means identical names, which are accepted automatically. Other matches are decided by written rules, then by a language model choosing only among listed candidates, then by Claude; each shows its confidence, who accepted it and why. Unmatched names are shown as printed.
about.datesNote: When a file states no date, its effective date is when the server says the file last changed. That can differ from the label on the source page: IESCO labels its schedule files {label}, but the files were last changed on {date}, so the schedule may have applied since then.

glossary: A published plan for when a feeder's power is to be switched off. This site shows schedules only; it never measures whether power actually went off.

architecture.title: From a utility's PDF to this page, every day
architecture.intro: Roshni is a small data platform. It collects published schedules and reports, checks and models them in a warehouse, matches names across sources and publishes this static site. Each step below is a command in one Python command-line tool, and GitHub Actions runs them in order every day.
architecture.flowHint: The lamps light in the order the data moves.

sources.title: Public sources
sources.body: Load-shedding schedules from IESCO and K-Electric, IESCO's planned-shutdown press releases, the PBS Census 2023, NEPRA's performance reports and approved news feeds. Only approved sources, and robots.txt is checked for every host.

snapshot.title: Polite snapshots
snapshot.body: A daily job fetches each source at most once a second, asks only for files that changed, and stores every new file once, with its SHA-256 hash and fetch time, on a separate branch.

parse.title: Parse and check
parse.body: One parser per source turns PDFs and spreadsheets into typed rows saved as Parquet. Rows that cannot be read go to quarantine with a reason, and expectation suites check every table.

warehouse.title: Warehouse
warehouse.body: SQL models build staging views, joins and marts in DuckDB, with tests on every model. The same models run unchanged on Databricks.

resolve.title: Match and analyse
resolve.body: Feeder names are matched across sources by name similarity. Exact matches are accepted; the rest are decided by written rules, then by a language model choosing only among listed candidates, then by Claude, each with a stored confidence. Descriptive statistics and a weekly summary follow: the model writes prose only, and every number in it is checked.

publish.title: Export and publish
publish.body: Tables are exported as versioned JSON, validated against a schema and typed into the site, which is built as static pages in English and Urdu and pushed to GitHub Pages.

architecture.runs: GitHub Actions is production: a daily snapshot job, then the publish job (parse, validate, build, match, report, export, site), and news feeds every three hours. A failure opens an issue. An Airflow DAG in Docker runs the same commands locally as a showcase.
architecture.checks: Golden tests on every parser, expectations on parsed tables and tests on every model. The site has its own gates: every number on the Karachi page is traced back to the export, translations are checked, pages are checked for accessibility in light and dark, and the browser's scheduled-dark logic is compared with Python's on the full export.
architecture.todayNote: Counts from the published files. Last updated:
principles: Schedules are not measurements: a scheduled window is never called an actual outage.
Nothing is invented: unreadable rows are quarantined with a reason, and known anomalies are flagged.
Times are shown in Pakistan time (UTC+5) and stored in UTC.
Approximate matches always show their confidence and who accepted them.
architecture.logosNote: Logos are trademarks of their owners, shown only to name the tools used (icons from Simple Icons, CC0). Tools without a published icon are shown as lettered tiles.
architecture.docsBody: Every model, column test and source, and the graph of how each table is built from the others.
architecture.codeBody: The pipeline, the warehouse models, the tests and this site, with the decisions behind them.

maker.kicker: The maker · the story behind Roshni
maker.title: The night it started
maker.intro: Roshni began the way so many evenings do in Pakistan: in the dark.

chapters.title: The lights went out again
chapters.body: Load shedding is part of life in my area of Islamabad. The fan slows, the Wi-Fi drops, the street goes quiet, and everyone asks the same two questions: was this planned, and when is it coming back?

chapters.title: The answers were all over the place
chapters.body: The power companies do publish schedules, but as a spreadsheet of six alternative plans, as PDFs and as press releases on different pages, while NEPRA's yearly reports say how many hours each company reported. Nothing put them side by side, and nothing kept the history.

chapters.title: So I built a pipeline
chapters.body: I'm a data engineer, so I treated it like any production data problem: collect politely every morning, parse and test every file, model it in a warehouse, match messy names across sources, and publish something anyone can read on a phone, in English and Urdu.

chapters.kicker: IV · Honest about what it knows
chapters.title: Plans, reports and the gap between them
chapters.body: Roshni shows schedules and reported figures, not measurements. It cannot tell you whether your feeder actually went dark. It can show what was planned, what was reported, and where the two disagree.

maker.finale: This page is the last lamp on the line.
